contexts.text: Before her online class, Sara noticed that her wireless mouse had a low battery. She plugged it in to charge. Next, she connected her laptop to the power supply and started it up. The class app was running slowly, so she checked whether an update was available. After the update, it ran normally. She downloaded the teacher's file to her laptop, completed the task and uploaded her answer. Downloading brought the file to her device; uploading sent her work to the class website.

Nora is an undergraduate studying history. During her first week on campus, she attended a lecture with a large group of students and a seminar with a small group. She took notes during the lecture, then discussed the topic in the seminar. Her tutor helped her plan an assignment and explained how to use the university library. Nora has not graduated yet. After her first degree, she may become a postgraduate and do research, but she has not decided. This week, her main aim is to understand her timetable.

These figures describe an invented company for language practice. Sales were 40 units in January, 50 in February and 60 in March. They rose steadily during those three months. In April, sales reached a peak of 90 units. There was a slight fall to 85 in May, followed by a sharper fall to 60 in June. Sales then remained stable at 60 in July and August. The report describes changes in sales, rather than giving advice about investing money.
